1.name: Lever body
1.note: Holds the master cylinder bore, the reservoir and the lever pivot.

2.name: Clamp half
2.note: Closes the lever body round the Ø22.2 handlebar, with the two clamp screws.

3.name: Lever blade
3.note: The lever you pull. The finger point is 80 mm from the pivot and the pushrod 22 mm, so it multiplies your force.

4.name: Pivot pin
4.note: The pivot the lever blade turns on.

5.name: Barrel nut
5.note: Holds the pushrod in the lever. It sits 22 mm from the pivot and sets the lever's reach.

6.name: Pushrod
6.note: Passes the lever's movement to the master piston, with a ball end so it can follow the lever's arc.

7.name: Master piston
7.note: The piston that writes the pressure. Its 78.5 mm² face pushes the oil towards the caliper.

8.name: Primary cup
8.note: The seal on the piston face. Until its lip passes the timing port no pressure can build, which is the free stroke.

9.name: Secondary seal
9.note: Seals the rear of the master piston so oil cannot escape past it.

10.name: Return spring
10.note: Pushes the piston and lever back when you let go.

11.name: Circlip
11.note: Holds the piston assembly in the bore against the return spring.

12.name: Dust boot
12.note: Keeps grit and water out of the bore round the pushrod.

13.name: Reservoir cap
13.note: Closes the oil reservoir and holds the bladder.

14.name: Bladder
14.note: A flexible diaphragm that lets the oil level change without letting air in as the pads wear.

15.name: Mineral brake oil
15.note: The fluid that carries the force. It does not compress, so what moves at the master piston moves at the caliper.

16.name: Compression nut
16.note: Screws into the lever body or the caliper and squeezes the olive onto the hose.

17.name: Olive
17.note: A brass ring that the nut crushes onto the hose to seal it.

18.name: Hose insert
18.note: A tube pressed into the hose end so the olive can grip it without closing the bore.

19.name: Hose
19.note: Carries the oil from lever to caliper. It swells a little under load, which adds to the softness of the lever after the pads touch.

20.name: Caliper half, inboard
20.note: The half of the caliper on the frame side, with one Ø22 piston bore.

21.name: Caliper half, outboard
21.note: The wheel-side half, with the other Ø22 bore. Oil passes between the halves across the sealed joint.

22.name: Caliper piston
22.note: The replica piston, one each side. Its 380 mm² face is about 4.8 times the master's, so a small stroke becomes a larger force.

23.name: Square seal
23.note: Seals each piston and is its return spring. It flexes as the piston moves, then pulls it back by the rollback, which sets the pad gap.

24.name: Pad
24.note: Friction lining on a steel back plate. The pistons press them onto the rotor.

25.name: Pad spring
25.note: Pushes the pads apart so they do not drag on the rotor when you release.

26.name: Pad pin
26.note: Holds the pads and spring in the caliper while letting the pads slide.

27.name: Rotor
27.note: The disc bolted to the wheel. The pads clamp it, and the friction turns the wheel's motion into heat.

28.name: O-ring
28.note: Seals the oil passage between the two caliper halves.

29.name: Clamp screw
29.note: Closes the clamp half onto the handlebar.
